title: Guidelines on Students with Gender Dysphoria
what_it_is: Guidelines on Students with Gender Dysphoria

sections.label: Medical treatment and parental consent
sections.summary: Medical treatment decisions rest with medical professionals, persons with gender dysphoria and family, with parental consent required for minors below 21.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Medical professionals recognise that each person with gender dysphoria is different.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: All medical treatment decisions, including the use of hormone replacement therapy, ultimately rest with medical professionals, the persons with gender dysphoria and their family.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Where minors are concerned – meaning anyone below the age of 21 – parental consent is required before any hormonal treatment can commence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Such medical decisions are beyond the purview of MOE or any educational institution.

sections.label: School rules and hormone therapy
sections.summary: Schools can exercise flexibility and make practical arrangements for students with gender dysphoria undergoing hormone therapy, consulting stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They are in place to help students cultivate self-discipline and a sense of responsibility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we recognise that students diagnosed with gender dysphoria and undergoing hormone therapy could face difficulties with certain school rules.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Where there are valid medical grounds, schools can exercise flexibility and work out practical arrangements for these students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The schools will consult and work closely with different stakeholders, including the relevant medical professionals, the students concerned and their parents, in putting in place these arrangements.

sections.label: Families uncomfortable with public airing
sections.summary: Family members, especially parents, are very uncomfortable with a public airing of their situation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our experience dealing with such cases is that the family members themselves, especially the parents, are very uncomfortable with a public airing of their situation.
